interactivePreview.title: Don't just memorize equations — test your chemical intuition
interactivePreview.subtitle: Every experiment on ChemLab KG pairs real laboratory footage with interactive concept checks that give you immediate, visual feedback.
interactivePreview.questionPrompt: During the electrolysis of water (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂), two gases collect in inverted test tubes above the electrodes. Which observation confirms that the gas in the cathode tube is hydrogen (H₂) and why does it have twice the volume?

options.label: It relights a glowing splint, and hydrogen atoms are larger than oxygen atoms.
options.feedback: Not quite! Relighting a glowing splint is the classic test for oxygen (O₂), not hydrogen. Also, gas volume at the same temperature and pressure depends on the number of molecules (Avogadro's law), not atomic size.

options.label: It burns with acharacteristic 'pop' sound near a flame, and each water molecule (H₂O) contains 2 hydrogen atoms per 1 oxygen atom.
options.feedback: Spot on! Hydrogen reacts rapidly with oxygen in air (2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O) producing a sharp 'pop'. Because H₂O has a 2:1 ratio of H to O, stoichiometry produces 2 moles of H₂ gas for every 1 mole of O₂.

options.label: It turns limewater milky, and hydrogen dissolves less in water than oxygen.
options.feedback: Turning limewater (Ca(OH)₂) milky is the test for carbon dioxide (CO₂), which forms insoluble calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).
